a usual setting of the state space is $\sX = [S]^d$, where $S$ is the number of states in each dimension.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated rate (jump to each single-coordinate-differing state at rate 1/d), each coordinate is a CTMC on S states with total jump rate (S-1)/d, whose exact law is p_t(b|a) = 1/S + e^{-St/d}(\delta_{ba} - 1/S). The displayed product instead puts mass e^{-t} + (1-e^{-t})/d on x_0^i and (1-e^{-t})/d on every state, which sums to e^{-t} + S(1-e^{-t})/d ≠ 1 unless S = d; neither the exponential rate nor the denominator is consistent with the stated rate matrix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix the normalization consistently, e.g. state the per-coordinate transition p_t(b|a) = 1/S + e^{-St/d}(\delta_{ba} - 1/S) for the given rate, or change the rate convention (e.g. 1/(S-1) per ordered jump) so the displayed closed form is correct.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised closed-form conditional distribution for the uniform discrete diffusion (used to present eq:discrete_diffusion_loss as practical) is not a probability law as stated; no labelled theorem depends on it.
issues.title: Uniform-rate closed-form conditional density is inconsistent with the stated rate matrix
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one displayed constant/rate convention restores the claim; no theorem, guarantee, or rate depends on this background display.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed Radon–Nikodym derivative does not depend on λ at all, while the stated transformed generator \gL^{h,λ}f = h^{-1}\gL(hf) - λf does; two different λ's would give the same derivative but different generators, which is impossible. The cited generalized Doob transform carries an extra factor exp(-∫_0^T λ_t(x_t)dt) in the exponent (and for λ ≠ h^{-1}(∂_t+\gL)h the transformed object is sub-Markovian, not 'another Markov process').
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the term -\int_0^T \lambda_t(x_t)\dif t into the exponent of eq:doob, matching the cited generalized Doob transform, and note sub-Markovianity unless λ is conservative.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:doob is false as stated for general λ; only the conservative specialization λ = h^{-1}\gL h (the case actually used downstream) survives after restoring the missing term.
issues.title: Generalized Doob's h-transform: Radon–Nikodym formula omits the killing term λ
issues.why_classification: A one-term correction to a quoted background formula restores consistency; the conservative case used by all later results is unaffected, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The middle expression h^{-1}\gL(hf) - h^{-1}f\gL h equals \gL f + h^{-1}Γ(h,f) only for the standard carré du champ Γ(h,f) = \gL(hf) - h\gL f - f\gL h. The formula printed in the theorem, h\gL(h^{-1}f) - f\gL h^{-1}, expands to \gL f + (h-1)f\gL h^{-1} - h^{-1}Γ_std(h,f), which is a different object: e.g. for \gL = ½∂² and h = e^x the claimed identity demands ½f'' + f' = ½f'' + e^{-x}(½f'' - f'), false in general. The displayed 'carré du champ operator' is therefore not the carré du champ and the stated equality fails.

issues.failure_explanation: The Courrège representation theorem invoked in the proof gives a positive semidefinite diffusion matrix; positive definiteness is not implied and is false for pure-jump generators. The paper's own novel models (the jump model of Sec. 6.2 and the α-stable Lévy-Itô model) set D ≡ 0, so as stated the theorem's coefficient condition excludes exactly the jump dynamics the paper advocates, and neither thm:general_levy nor its rigorous version thm:courrege_form is correct as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the last equality is by Dynkin's formula (\cref{thm:dynkin}).

issues.failure_explanation: The h-transform change of measure (Palmowski–Rolski Thm 4.2, as cited) carries the multiplicative endpoint factor η_{T-t}(\cev x_t)/η_T(\cev x_0), exactly as in the paper's own eq:doob. The proof drops it by an application of Dynkin's formula 'η_{T-s}∂_s log η_{T-s} = ∂_s η_{T-s}'-type cancellation that is valid only in expectation, not along paths; a pure exponential of a bounded drift integral is generally not a martingale (e.g. on a two-state chain with nonconstant bounded η its expectation is strictly below 1 for small t), so the displayed quantity is not a Radon–Nikodym derivative, \sQ as defined is not a probability measure, and the claim that (\cev x_t) is governed by \gK_t under it is unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the multiplicative factor η_{T-t}(\cev x_t)/η_T(\cev x_0) from the cited theorem (and its inverse in d\P/d\sQ), deleting the invalid pathwise Dynkin step; in the proof of cor:change_of_measure evaluate the endpoint term by Dynkin's formula in expectation, which reproduces the same \mathfrak L[η].
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:change_of_measure_app's displayed derivative (and the reciprocal claim) is wrong; the KL identity of cor:change_of_measure and the error bounds survive because they only use expectations, and are re-obtained once the endpoint factor is restored.
issues.title: Radon–Nikodym derivative in the change-of-measure theorem is not a valid density
issues.why_classification: The repair is the standard, local reinstatement of the h-transform endpoint factor already present in the paper's own Theorem thm:doob; every downstream guarantee (KL bound, error bound, loss function) is preserved unchanged.
